Working with the manually segmented images, predict for the prosome and carbon content using a linear regression model and a random forest model. Select the best alternative model to apply to images with "bad" segmentations or images that are not classified as Calanus/with visible lipid sacs.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(randomForest)
library(randomForestExplainer)

```

1. Load the manual segmentations + Ecotaxa morpho traits then calculate traits
N = 1,806
```{r}
# The output files of the model training
res.prosome <-  read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/model_resnet34_prosomeUVP6_deamundp1_v2/prediction_prosome_uvp6_20251204.csv") %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename, ".png")) %>% 
  select(object_id, prosome_pixels = prosome_pixels_annotated,
         prosomeMajor = prosome_major_annotated,)

res.lipid.crop <-  read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/model_resnet34_lipidcropUVP6_deamundp1_v2/prediction_lipids_uvp6_20251204.csv") %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename, ".png")) %>% 
  select(object_id, lipid_pixels = lipid_pixels_annotated,
         lipidMajor = lipid_major_annotated)

# UVP6 Resolution
uvpRes <- 0.073

# Conversion factor to get total lipid mg C from total lipid mg used in Schmidt et al. 2018 based on 36-carbon chain lengths in (Kattner & Graeve 1991) 
lambda <- (36*12) / (36*12 + 2*36 + 2*16)

# Conversion factor from mm3 -> WW -> C
# If density asssumed as 1, the value below is the Carbon % Wet weight
# 0.09 is the average for all calanoid copepod species
# 0.0766 is the average for calanoid copepod species except lipid sac forming species
prosomeWW2C <- 0.07666 # 0.07666


# inner join to retain only images that have both segmentations
df.segmented <- inner_join(res.prosome, res.lipid.crop,
                           by = "object_id") %>% 

# Calculate traits from pixels
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid_pixels * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_length_mm = prosomeMajor * uvpRes) %>% 
  # Calculate minor axis based on prosome/lipid area and major axis (in pixels)
  mutate(minor_derived = (prosome_pixels / (pi * prosomeMajor/2)) * 2) %>% 
    # Calculate biovolume of prosome approximated as spheroid
  mutate(prosome_biovolume_mm3 = 4/3 * pi * 
           (prosomeMajor/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2)) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid sac volume based on Tarling et al. (2022) eq1 derived from Miller et al. (1998) note that this is  based on cyclindrical volume approximation. According to Miller et al. (1998) the oblate spheroid volume approximation is less accurate
  mutate(lipid_volume_mm3 = 
           (pi * lipid_area_mm2 ^ 2)/(4 * lipidMajor * uvpRes)) %>% 
  
# (Calculate lipid carbon based on area following Vogedes et al. 2010 with coefficients for 3 Arctic Calanus species
  mutate(totallipid_mass_mg = 0.197 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.38)) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mg = 0.167 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.42)) %>%  
  
  # Calculate lipid carbon mass
  mutate(lipid_mass_mgC = totallipid_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mgC = waxester_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  
   # Calculate the carbon content of the prosome excluding the lipid sac
  mutate(structural_carbon_mgC = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 
           prosomeWW2C) %>% 
  
  mutate(prosome_total_mgC = structural_carbon_mgC + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid fullness as % carbon in lipid sac WE
  mutate(lipid_fullness = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_total_mgC * 100) %>% 
  
  # Streamline variables
  select(object_id, prosome_total_mgC, structural_carbon_mgC,
         waxester_mass_mgC, lipid_fullness)


# Load and combine the Ecotaxa morphotraits
load("C:/Sync/UVP6_Data/Amund_UVP6_plankton_20251125.RData")
df.segmented <- df.segmented %>% 
  left_join(Amund_UVP6 %>% 
              select(object_id,
                     Major = object_major, Minor = object_minor, 
                     Perim = object_perim., Feret = object_feret, 
                     Area = object_area, Elongation = object_elongation,
                     VerSym = object_symetriev, VerSym2 = object_symetrievc, 
                     Circ = object_circ., Thickr = object_thickr, 
                     MeanGrey = object_mean, MedGrey = object_median,
                     HistGrey75 = object_histcum3, SdevGrey = object_stddev, 
                     SkewGrey = object_skew, Fractal = object_fractal, 
                     PerimFeret = object_perimferet, 
                     PerimMajor = object_perimmajor),
            by = "object_id")

rm(res.prosome, res.lipid.crop, Amund_UVP6, Amund_UVP6_meta, taxamatch)
```

# 2. Regression models
## Loop through predictors
```{r, eval=FALSE}
# OLS regression model function
getRegressionModel <- function(df, X, Y, base = "10") {
  trait.sub <- df %>% 
    filter(!is.na(get(X)) & !is.na(get(Y))) %>% 
    relocate(X, Y)
  
  if (nrow(trait.sub) > 3) {
    # Calculate OLS
    if(base == "10") {
      reg <- lm(log10(get(Y)) ~ log10(get(X)), data = trait.sub)
    } else if (base == "e") {
      reg <- lm(log(get(Y)) ~ log(get(X)), data = trait.sub)
    } else if (base == "none") {
      reg <- lm(get(Y) ~ get(X), data = trait.sub)
    } else {
      stop("Error: Please select either base 10, e, or none.")
    }
    
    reg.results <- data.frame(X = X,  Y = Y, 
                              a = reg$coefficients[1],
                              b = reg$coefficients[2],
                              n = nrow(trait.sub),
                              R2 = summary(reg)$adj.r.squared,
                              RSE = summary(reg)$sigma,
                              pval = getpval(summary(reg)$fstatistic), 
                              model = "OLS", base = as.character(base),
                              minX = min(trait.sub[,1]), maxX = max(trait.sub[,1]))
  } else {
    reg.results <- data.frame(X = X,  Y = Y, 
                              a = NA, b = NA, n = nrow(trait.sub),
                              R2 = NA, RSE = NA, pval = NA, 
                              model = "OLS", base = as.character(base),
                              minX = NA, maxX = NA)
  }
  
  return(reg.results %>% 
           remove_rownames())
}

getpval <- function(x){ 
  p <- pf(x[1],x[2],x[3],lower.tail = F) 
  attributes(p) <- NULL
  return(p)
}


allom_sub <- df.segmented %>% 
  # select(c(structural_carbon_mgC, waxester_mass_mgC, Major:PerimMajor))
  select(structural_carbon_mgC, waxester_mass_mgC, Area, Major, Perim, Feret)

# prepare data frame of models to test
reg.models <- data.frame( modelNum = c(1:9),
                          X = c("structural_carbon_mgC", 
                                "Area", "Major", 
                                "Perim", "Feret",
                                "Area", "Major", 
                                "Perim", "Feret"),
                          Y = c("waxester_mass_mgC", 
                                "waxester_mass_mgC", "waxester_mass_mgC", 
                                "waxester_mass_mgC", "waxester_mass_mgC",
                                "structural_carbon_mgC", "structural_carbon_mgC",
                                "structural_carbon_mgC", "structural_carbon_mgC") ) %>% 
  mutate(model = "OLS", 
         base = "none")

# survey linear regression models
reg.results <- data.frame()
for (i in c(1:nrow(reg.models))){
  reg.results <- bind_rows(reg.results, 
                           getRegressionModel(allom_sub, 
                                              reg.models$X[i], reg.models$Y[i],
                                              base = reg.models$base[i]))
}

# Area is the best predictor for the regression model
lipid.reg.area <- lm(waxester_mass_mgC ~ Area,
                data = df.segmented)
prosome.reg.area <- lm(structural_carbon_mgC ~ Area,
                data = df.segmented)

(lipid.reg.area.sum <- summary(lipid.reg.area))
(prosome.reg.area.sum <- summary(prosome.reg.area))

paste("Lipid RMSR:", sqrt(mean(residuals(lipid.reg.area)^2)) )
paste("Prosome RMSR:", sqrt(mean(residuals(prosome.reg.area)^2)) )


df.segmented$reg_pred_prosome <- predict(prosome.reg.area, 
                                       newdata = df.segmented %>% select(Area))
df.segmented$reg_pred_lipid <- predict(lipid.reg.area, 
                                       newdata = df.segmented %>% select(Area))

```

# 3. Random forest model
```{r}

# subset data to simply be StructCarbon, WaxEster, + predictors
df_for_rf <- df.segmented %>% 
  select(c(structural_carbon_mgC, waxester_mass_mgC, Major:PerimMajor))

# Random forest regression on structural carbon mass
set.seed(888)
rf.model.prosome <- randomForest(structural_carbon_mgC ~ .,
                      data = df_for_rf %>% 
                        select(-waxester_mass_mgC), 
                      importance = TRUE, proximity = TRUE)

# Try random forest regression on lipid (wax ester) mass
set.seed(888)
rf.model.lipid <- randomForest(waxester_mass_mgC ~ .,
                      data = df_for_rf %>% 
                        select(-c(structural_carbon_mgC)), 
                      importance = TRUE, proximity = TRUE)
rf.model.prosome 
rf.model.lipid 

plot(rf.model.prosome)
plot(rf.model.lipid)


# save(rf.model.prosome, rf.model.lipid,
#      file = "functions/random_forest_carbon_trait_models.RData")
```


### Get RMSE of random forest model
```{r, eval=FALSE}
calc_r2 <- function(x, y) {
  if (is.numeric(x) && is.numeric(y) && length(na.omit(x)) > 1 && length(na.omit(y)) > 1) {
    df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)
    model <- lm(y ~ x, data = df, na.action = na.omit)
    return(round(summary(model)$r.squared, 3))
  } else {
    return(NA) # Return NA if column is not numeric or has insufficient data
  }
}

df.segmented$rf_pred_prosome <- predict(rf.model.prosome, newdata = df.segmented %>% 
                             select(Major:PerimMajor))
df.segmented$rf_pred_lipid <- predict(rf.model.lipid, newdata = df.segmented %>% 
                             select(Major:PerimMajor))

# Calculate RMSE
rf_rmse_prosome = sqrt(mean((df.segmented$structural_carbon_mgC - 
                               df.segmented$rf_pred_prosome)^2))
rf_rmse_lipid = sqrt(mean((df.segmented$waxester_mass_mgC - 
                             df.segmented$rf_pred_lipid)^2))

# Plot comparison
cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(df.segmented, aes(x = structural_carbon_mgC, 
                             y = rf_pred_prosome)) +
    geom_abline() +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    annotate("text", 
             x = max(df.segmented$structural_carbon_mgC, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(df.segmented$rf_pred_prosome, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(df.segmented$structural_carbon_mgC,      
                                             df.segmented$rf_pred_prosome)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5) +
    xlab("Structural carbon - segmentation") + 
    ylab("Structural carbon - random forest"),
  
   ggplot(df.segmented, aes(x = waxester_mass_mgC, 
                              y = rf_pred_lipid)) +
    geom_abline() +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    annotate("text", 
             x = max(df.segmented$waxester_mass_mgC, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(df.segmented$rf_pred_lipid, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(df.segmented$waxester_mass_mgC,
                                             df.segmented$rf_pred_lipid)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5) +
    xlab("Wax ester - segmentation") + 
    ylab("Wax ester - random forest"),
  
  labels = "auto"
)

#        height = 4, width = 6, units = "in")

```

### importance of parameters
Generally, the RF models mainly use area, and dimensions (major, feret, minor, perim) to model both prosome and lipid mass. Is this just a fancy allometric scaling model? The lipid mass predictor does value Fractal more which indicates that there is something more to this.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
cowplot::plot_grid(
  plot_multi_way_importance(model.prosome, size_measure = "no_of_nodes"),
  plot_multi_way_importance(model.prosome, x_measure = "mse_increase", y_measure = "node_purity_increase", size_measure = "p_value", no_of_labels = 5),
  labels = "auto")

# ggsave("figures/UVP6_rf_structural_importance.png",
#        height = 4, width = 9, units = "in")


cowplot::plot_grid(
  plot_multi_way_importance(model.lipid, size_measure = "no_of_nodes"),
  plot_multi_way_importance(model.lipid, x_measure = "mse_increase", y_measure = "node_purity_increase", size_measure = "p_value", no_of_labels = 5),
  labels = "auto")

# ggsave("figures/UVP6_rf_waxester_importance.png",
#        height = 4, width = 9, units = "in")
```

## Compare R2 of regression model vs random forest vs CNN model
```{r}
summary(lm(structural_carbon_mgC ~ reg_pred_lipid, # Regression of Area based
           data = df.segmented))
summary(lm(structural_carbon_mgC ~ rf_pred_lipid, # random forest of Area based
           data = df.segmented))
summary(lm(structural_carbon_mgC ~ CNN_pred_lipid, # CNN based
           data = df.segmented))


summary(lm(waxester_mass_mgC ~ reg_pred_lipid, # Regression of Area based
           data = df.segmented))
summary(lm(waxester_mass_mgC ~ rf_pred_lipid, # random forest based
           data = df.segmented))
summary(lm(waxester_mass_mgC ~ CNN_pred_lipid, # CNN based
           data = df.segmented))
```
